title: 〜ばそれまでだ / 〜たらそれまでだ
romaji: ba sore made da / tara sore made da
meaning: if …, that is the end of it; once …, it is all over
simpleExplanation: 〜ばそれまでだ means "if X happens, everything is finished and nothing more can be done". それまで = "up to there". It shows that all the effort or value before X becomes meaningless: 死んでしまえばそれまでだ (once you die, that's it). A common variation is 〜と言ってしまえばそれまでだ ("if you put it that way, there's nothing more to say").
whenUsed: Both speech and writing. Typical topics: money and possessions, passwords and data, preparation and health, arguments. It often follows a concessive clause like どんなに〜ても or いくら〜ても.
formation: Set phrase: 〜と言ってしまえばそれまでだ(が)
Often: いくら/どんなに〜ても、〜ばそれまでだ

parts.text: どんなに財産があっても

parts.role: that is the end of it

diagram.translation: However much wealth you have, once you die, that is the end of it.

examples.ja: どんなに財産があっても、死んでしまえばそれまでだ。
examples.reading: どんなにざいさんがあっても、しんでしまえばそれまでだ。
examples.en: However much wealth you have, once you die, that is the end of it.
examples.note: The classic proverb-like use: wealth means nothing after death.

examples.ja: パスワードを忘れたらそれまでだから、必ずメモしておこう。
examples.reading: パスワードをわすれたらそれまでだから、かならずメモしておこう。
examples.en: If you forget the password, that is it, so be sure to write it down.
examples.note: たらそれまでだ with a practical warning about passwords.

examples.ja: いくら準備しても、当日に体調を崩せばそれまでだ。
examples.reading: いくらじゅんびしても、とうじつにたいちょうをくずせばそれまでだ。
examples.en: However much you prepare, if you fall ill on the day, it is all over.
examples.note: Preparation is wasted if you fall ill on the day: a lament about fragility.

examples.ja: 運が悪かったと言ってしまえばそれまでだが、対策は必要だ。
examples.reading: うんがわるかったといってしまえばそれまでだが、たいさくはひつようだ。
examples.en: If you put it down to bad luck there is nothing more to say, but we still need countermeasures.
examples.note: 〜と言ってしまえばそれまでだが is a set rhetorical move.

examples.ja: どんなに高価な時計でも、落として壊せばそれまでだ。
examples.reading: どんなにこうかなとけいでも、おとしてこわせばそれまでだ。
examples.en: However expensive the watch, drop it and break it and that is the end of it.
examples.note: どんなに〜でも + ばそれまでだ.

similarGrammar.difference: "Once X happens, an unstoppable bad process follows". ばそれまでだ says things simply end; たら最後 says things go from bad to worse.
Same ば but a completely different meaning: "precisely because".
"I will simply …": a calm alternative. それまでだ is about an ending, not an alternative.

commonMistakes.wrong: パスワードを忘れればそれまでだから、書いておこう。
commonMistakes.right: パスワードを忘れたらそれまでだから、書いておこう。
commonMistakes.why: Both ば and たら are grammatical, but with a momentary event like 忘れる, たら sounds more natural in speech.

commonMistakes.wrong: 勉強すればそれまでだ。
commonMistakes.right: 勉強しなければそれまでだ。
commonMistakes.why: The condition must be the undesirable event that ends everything; 勉強する is not such an event.

commonMistakes.wrong: 彼が来ればそれまでだ。（意味：彼が来れば十分だ）
commonMistakes.why: それまでだ does not mean "that is enough"; it means "it is all over".

usageNotes: The clause before it is the fatal event: dying, forgetting, breaking, losing.
〜と言ってしまえばそれまでだ is used to admit that a blunt summary is true before adding a "but".
The tone is resigned or cautionary, which is why it pairs naturally with advice (〜ておこう).
jlptTips: Look for いくら / どんなに〜ても before the blank and a fatal event in the ば clause.
Distractors: たら最後, ばこそ, までだ. たら最後 needs an ongoing bad consequence in the second clause; ばそれまでだ ends the sentence.
In 文法形式の判断 the blank is usually the whole それまでだ; do not confuse with それきりだ.
